sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Stickman Video Director is an AI agent skill for Claude Code, Codex and similar agents that turns a topic, article or script into a finished stickman animation video, with voiceover, captions and sound effects. It offers 16 styles and two ways to make the visuals.
sixtySeconds.problem: Making animated explainer videos for faceless YouTube, Shorts or TikTok channels normally needs animation software or paid video tools. This skill lets your coding agent write the script, prepare assets and produce the video for you, with you approving the script and a preview first.
whoFor: Creators running faceless YouTube, Shorts or TikTok channels
Claude Code or Codex users who want to use spare quota for video
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you already use a capable coding agent and want stickman explainer videos without After Effects. The README recommends Codex or Claude Code for results close to its samples.
requirements: An AI agent that can read and write files and run commands (Codex or Claude Code recommended)
Node.js/npm and Git for terminal installation
Model Engine: access to a video generation platform such as Google Flow
Code Engine: image generation and text-to-speech tools your agent can use

overview: There are two modes. Model Engine (A) turns your idea into a storyboard and scene prompts for video generation models such as Google Flow, then generates the clips manually or through the agent's browser. Code Engine (B) has the agent create layered character and scene assets, write animation code and render the whole video locally, so it uses no video model credits.

You can start from an idea, an article, a link or a full script, in 16:9 or 9:16, with captions, voiceover, background music and sound effects. The agent first shows you a script (and, in Code Engine, a 20-second preview with audio) and only continues after you approve it. A Thumbnail and Publishing Kit then creates a thumbnail, title, description and pinned comment.

The skill is MIT licensed and free, but the services you connect cost money: your agent's plan, video generation credits in Model Engine, and any image or speech APIs. You don't need to write code or own an expensive GPU; your computer's performance mainly affects speed.

steps.title: Send this to your AI agent
steps.body: On first use the agent checks the setup and helps install anything missing.
steps.code:
Help me install this skill:
https://github.com/kaomei/stickman-video-director
After installation, read SKILL.md and tell me you're ready.

tutorial.title: Make your first stickman video with the Code Engine
tutorial.useCase: Turn an article into a narrated stickman video rendered locally by your agent.
setup: Codex or Claude Code with image generation and text-to-speech tools available

steps.title: Send the Code Engine prompt to your agent
steps.body: Adapt the topic, length and style.
steps.code:
Use Code Engine (B) to turn the following topic or article into an engaging stickman video:
[Paste an article, a news story, or a link, or describe your topic]
Requirements: 16:9 landscape, 8 minutes, style B1 "Minimal Line Art," with voiceover, captions, and sound effects.
First, check that the local tools for image generation and rendering are set up. Then provide a complete script and a preview of the opening 20 seconds with audio.
After I approve both, automatically prepare all assets, write the code, and render the complete video locally.

steps.title: Approve the script and 20-second preview
steps.body: Ask for changes to any section you don't like before approving.

steps.title: Create the thumbnail and publishing text
steps.code: Create a thumbnail, video title, description, and pinned comment for the video we just made, using the approved visual style.

tutorial.expected: The agent prepares the assets, animation, captions and audio, renders the full video locally and gives you a preview, followed by a matching thumbnail, title, description and pinned comment.

troubleshooting.problem: Installation times out cloning the repository
troubleshooting.solution: Retry with SKILLS_CLONE_TIMEOUT_MS=1200000, or clone locally first and run npx skills add ./stickman-video-director --skill directing-stickman-videos.

troubleshooting.problem: Characters look different between clips (Model Engine)
troubleshooting.solution: Add a stick-figure character reference image and reuse it for later clips.
Use an agent with strong coding ability such as Codex or Claude Code; the samples used Google Flow (A) and Codex (B).
